findings.claim: Clause 1.1.2 defines Confidential Information broadly across formats and scope. However, it lacks standard carve-outs/exceptions (e.g., publicly available information, independently developed information, or rightfully received third-party information), making the scope overly broad for the receiving party.

evidence.quotedText:
15. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
15.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.
15.2 Any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach or termination, shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended from time to time).
15.3 The arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator mutually appointed by the Parties. The seat and venue of arbitration shall be Mumbai, India, and the language of arbitration shall be English. The arbitral award shall be final and binding on the Parties.
15.4 Subject to Clause 15.2, the courts at Mumbai shall have exclusive jurisdiction in respect of any matter arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including for interim relief under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

10. TERM AND TERMINATION
10.1 This Agreement shall commence on the date first written above and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years (the "Term"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Agreement.
10.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party.
10.3 Notwithstanding termination or expiry of this Agreement, the confidentiality obligations under this Agreement shall survive and continue to bind the Receiving Party for a period of three (3) years from the date of such termination or expiry; provided that with respect to any Confidential Information constituting a trade secret under applicable law, the obligations of confidentiality shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.

15.2 Any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach or termination, shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended from time to time).

findings.claim: Clause 10.1 establishes a term of two years, and Clause 10.3 specifies that confidentiality obligations survive for three years post-termination, with indefinite survival for trade secrets as long as they remain trade secrets.
